text:
Nashville has won six straight, and it hasn't been subtle about how. Juuse Saros, who finished last season 10.2 goals below expected, is at +9.2 this season and .937 with 6.3 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. The chances only half back the streak: 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) during it. In Anaheim on Wednesday they had only 41% of the expected goals and won 4-2 anyway, the night Roman Josi reached 800 career points.

Vegas is the steadier version of the same story. Four straight wins, outscoring teams 14-7, and the chances back it with 54% of the expected goals. The Golden Knights closed their week with a 5-3 win over Utah in which they took 68% of the chances, and Ivan Barbashev, in Jesse Granger's words for The Athletic, is "officially out of the slump." Vegas plays without Noah Hanifin. Over the season the Golden Knights have the better five-on-five share (52% to 47%) and allow 2.73 expected goals per 60 to Nashville's 3.19. Our playoff odds have Vegas at 98% and Nashville at 67%.

The October meeting went 5-2 Vegas, though by the chances it was closer to a coin flip: Vegas deserved to win it 46% of the time. Adin Hill is projected in the other net, at +1.8 goals saved above expected after a rough -15.0 last season.

This is also Nashville's first stretch without Matthew Wood, traded to Seattle on Nov 1 for Shane Wright, and Jonathan Marchessault is off the out list and day-to-day. Filip Forsberg has two goals in a 3-0 win in Los Angeles behind him, Steven Stamkos just entered the all-time top five in power-play goals, and Jayden Struble has four points in ten games on chances that have actually gone up. For Vegas, Jack Eichel is on a four-game point streak at 76% for a point tonight, Mitch Marner is at 74%, and Brayden McNabb is one point from 200.
headline: Predators chase seven straight in Vegas
